name: Engine oil and filter
interval: Check monthly; change as specified in the owner's manual
description: Check the oil level on level ground using the procedure in your owner's manual. Use the correct oil grade and replace the filter at the specified service interval.
benefit: Supports lubrication and helps reduce engine wear.
difficulty: Basic level check; service change varies by vehicle
warning: Seek help if oil pressure warning lights stay on, the level drops repeatedly, or a major leak appears.

name: Tyre pressure
interval: Check monthly and before long journeys, when tyres are cold
description: Use a reliable pressure gauge and compare readings with the vehicle placard or owner's manual. Do not use the maximum pressure printed on the tyre sidewall as the normal target.
benefit: Correct pressure supports handling, tyre life, and fuel efficiency.
warning: Have repeated pressure loss, bulges, or visible damage inspected promptly.

name: Tyre tread and condition
description: Look for uneven wear, cracks, cuts, embedded objects, and tread wear indicators. Check all tyres, including the spare if fitted.
benefit: Good tyre condition improves grip and helps reduce the risk of a tyre failure.
warning: Do not drive on a tyre with a bulge, exposed cords, or serious damage.

name: Brake system
interval: Pay attention during every drive; inspect during scheduled servicing
description: Notice changes in pedal feel, pulling to one side, vibration, grinding, or squealing. Brake components should be inspected by a qualified technician.
benefit: Maintains stopping performance and road safety.
warning: If braking is reduced, a warning light appears, or grinding is severe, stop safely and arrange professional help.

name: Coolant level and condition
interval: Check according to the owner's manual, only when the engine is cold
description: Check the coolant reservoir level when the engine is cold. Use only the specified coolant mixture and never open a hot cooling system.
benefit: Helps control engine temperature and protect against corrosion.
warning: Never remove a radiator cap while hot. Repeated overheating or coolant loss needs professional attention.

name: Battery and terminals
interval: Inspect every few months and before long trips
description: Look for secure mounting, corrosion around terminals, and signs of damage. Avoid shorting the terminals and follow the manufacturer's safety instructions.
benefit: Supports reliable starting and stable electrical operation.
difficulty: Visual check; testing is best done with suitable equipment
warning: A swollen, leaking, or unusually hot battery should be handled by a professional.

name: Exterior lights and indicators
interval: Check weekly and before night journeys
description: Test headlights, tail lights, brake lights, hazard lights, and indicators. Clean lenses and replace failed bulbs with the correct type.
benefit: Helps you see and helps other road users understand your actions.
difficulty: Easy with assistance for brake lights
warning: Repair failed brake lights or headlights promptly; avoid night driving when visibility is unsafe.

name: Wiper blades and washer fluid
interval: Inspect monthly and before rainy periods
description: Check for cracked rubber, streaking, chatter, or missed areas. Refill the washer reservoir with suitable fluid and keep the windscreen clean.
benefit: Maintains visibility in rain, dust, and road spray.
warning: Replace blades if visibility remains poor after cleaning.

name: Engine air filter
interval: Inspect at scheduled service; replace as specified for the vehicle and conditions
description: A clean air filter allows the engine to receive the air it needs. Dusty roads may require more frequent inspection, but follow the manual's guidance.
benefit: Supports normal engine operation and helps keep dust out of the intake system.
difficulty: Varies by vehicle; consult the manual
warning: Have the intake inspected if the filter housing is damaged or the engine runs poorly.

name: Cabin air filter
interval: Replace at the interval in the owner's manual; inspect sooner in dusty conditions
description: The cabin filter helps reduce dust and particles entering through the ventilation system. Location and replacement procedure vary by model.
benefit: Supports cabin airflow and passenger comfort.
warning: If ventilation remains weak or smells persist after replacement, seek further inspection.

name: Belts and hoses
description: Look for visible cracks, fraying, swelling, leaks, or loose connections where safe to do so. Some components are difficult to see and need workshop inspection.
benefit: Helps identify wear that could lead to breakdowns.
difficulty: Visual check; replacement is a technician's task
warning: A damaged drive belt, leaking hose, or rapidly rising engine temperature needs prompt attention.

name: Transmission fluid
interval: Check or replace only according to the vehicle-specific procedure
description: Transmission designs differ. Some have dipsticks while others require special tools and temperature-specific procedures. Use only the specified fluid.
benefit: Supports correct transmission operation and component protection.
warning: Slipping, harsh shifts, burning smells, or fluid leaks should be checked by a qualified technician.

name: Steering system
interval: Notice changes while driving; inspect during scheduled servicing
description: Pay attention to unusual steering effort, vibration, clunks, or a vehicle that wanders. Some vehicles use electric steering and have no fluid reservoir.
warning: Sudden loss of steering assistance or serious looseness requires stopping safely and seeking help.

name: Suspension and shock absorbers
interval: Inspect during routine service and after severe impacts
description: Notice excessive bouncing, uneven tyre wear, knocking noises, or fluid leaking from shock absorbers. Suspension checks may require lifting equipment.
benefit: Supports stable handling, comfort, and tyre contact with the road.
warning: Severe instability, broken parts, or a wheel that appears misaligned needs urgent inspection.

name: Spark plugs (petrol engines)
interval: Replace according to engine and plug specifications
description: Spark plugs and replacement intervals vary by engine design and plug type. Misfires, difficult starting, or poor running can have several causes and need diagnosis.
benefit: Helps maintain efficient combustion and smooth engine operation.
difficulty: Vehicle dependent; correct tools and torque are important
warning: A flashing engine warning light or severe misfire should be checked promptly.

name: Fuel leaks and fuel cap
interval: Look for warning signs during routine checks
description: Notice fuel smells, visible wet patches, or a loose or damaged fuel cap. Never smoke or create sparks around suspected fuel leaks.
benefit: Supports safe operation and can help prevent fuel-system faults.
difficulty: Visual awareness; repairs require a professional
warning: If you suspect a fuel leak, stop the engine when safe, keep away from ignition sources, and seek assistance.

name: Emergency kit and spare tyre
interval: Check monthly and before long trips
description: Confirm the spare tyre, jack, wheel tool, warning triangle, torch, first-aid supplies, and other locally appropriate items are present and usable.
benefit: Helps you respond more safely to a breakdown or roadside problem.
warning: Never change a wheel beside moving traffic or work under a vehicle supported only by a jack.

name: Windscreen and mirrors
description: Keep glass and mirrors clean and check for cracks, loose mirrors, or obstructions to the driver's view. Adjust mirrors before moving.
benefit: Improves awareness of traffic and hazards around the vehicle.
warning: Damage that obstructs the driver's view or affects structural integrity needs prompt professional assessment.
